tables.name: users
tables.description: One row per signed-in user. Only one row exists for the MVP (the hardcoded 'user'), but boards/cards are modeled as belonging to a user so multi-user support does not require a schema change later.
tables.note: No password column. Part 4's login check is a hardcoded in-memory comparison, not a DB lookup - adding a password column now would be unused schema. Add one when real credential storage is actually needed.

tables.name: boards
tables.description: One row per user's Kanban board. Only one board per user for the MVP, enforced by application logic (not a schema constraint), matching CLAUDE.md's stated limitation.

tables.name: columns
tables.description: The fixed Kanban columns for a board. Rows are seeded once and never added to or removed from by the application - only 'name' is ever updated (rename). There is deliberately no API to create or delete a column.

columns.name: key
columns.note: Fixed internal identifier (e.g. 'todo'). Never changes, never exposed as editable.

columns.name: name
columns.note: User-editable display label. This is the only field the rename endpoint (Part 6) may update.

seed_data.description: Seeded once per board at backend startup (Part 6), matching the mock data already used by the frontend (Part 3) exactly.

tables.name: cards
tables.description: Individual Kanban cards. Freely created, edited, moved (across columns and reordered within a column), and deleted.

columns.name: order
columns.note: Position within column_id, 0-indexed. Resequenced on every move (Part 6).

tables.name: messages
tables.description: AI chat history for a board. Added now (Part 5) even though unused until Part 9, so the schema doesn't need a second sign-off round when chat is implemented.

not_modeled_as_tables.reason: Part 4 deliberately stores sessions in an in-memory Python dict, not SQLite. Single process, single container; a restart losing sessions is an accepted MVP limitation. See docs/database.md.
